title: NERC Reliability Standards for Data Centers and Crypto Loads Pass Final Ballot, Advance to Board Review
key_facts: NERC, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, announced on 15 Oct that proposed standards for data centers, AI sites and crypto operations passed their final stakeholder ballot.
They go next to NERC's Board of Trustees, then to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for approval.
The package has three new computational-load standards and revisions to two interconnection standards.
They would apply to sites with at least 50 MW of connected load supplied at 100 kV or above, up from an earlier 20 MW and 60 kV proposal.
Operators would have to follow grid operators' operating instructions unless physically impossible or unsafe or unlawful.
FERC's 16 July directive requires NERC to file initial standards by 31 Dec 2026.
Owners would share grid-modelling data, and keep fault and disturbance records.
quote_evidence: The standards and associated implementation plans will next go before NERC's Board of Trustees for adoption, followed by submission to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for U.S. regulatory approval, the organization said in its announcement.
The threshold is narrower than NERC's initial registration proposal: the minimum load and voltage criteria increased from 20 MW and 60 kV to 50 MW and 100 kV following stakeholder comments.
why_it_matters_hint: Big data centers can disturb the power grid, and the first national rules to make them behave like other major grid users are close.
notes: Standards are proposals until the board and FERC approve.
